skill.name: volcano
skill.description: Retrieve Japanese volcano eruption bulletins, warnings, alert levels, and commentary from public Japan Meteorological Agency data without authentication.
skill.summary: Check JMA volcano reports and match volcano names while preserving publication times and reporting unavailable data.
skill.author: tahodev

security_audit.summary: All 32 static findings are false positives involving Markdown syntax, intended public JMA requests, a documentation link, or readable multilingual text. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential access, or data exfiltration. One semantic finding identifies incorrect residential hazard classification for level 3 alerts.

remediation.issue: The guidance classifies all level 3 and higher warnings as affecting residential areas.
remediation.suggestion: Correct SKILL.md line 78 to distinguish mountain entry restrictions from residential measures. Use each official warning's stated affected area and JMA level definitions.

content.user_title: Check Japanese Volcano Reports from JMA
content.value_statement: Japanese volcano bulletins, warnings, and commentary are distributed across separate public feeds. This skill guides retrieval and interpretation with volcano names and publication times.
actual_capabilities: Retrieve eruption bulletins from the documented public JMA feed.
Read eruption warning labels and continuation or change conditions.
Retrieve volcano commentary headlines, publication times, and recency flags.
Match volcano identifiers with Japanese names, English names, and coordinates.
Sort reports by publication time and explain that older warnings may remain active.
Distinguish successful empty responses from unavailable data and report retrieval failures.
limitations: Requires network access and a tool capable of retrieving the public feeds; it supplies instructions rather than a standalone application.
Endpoint observations date from September 19, 2026, and do not guarantee current availability or continuous monitoring.
Undersea volcano data, earthquake reports, tsunami reports, and weather warnings are outside this skill's scope.
A referenced shared checklist is not included in the reviewed package, and residential hazard guidance needs correction before safety-sensitive use.

prompt_templates.title: Check Eruption Bulletins
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the JMA eruption feed for published bulletins. Include publication times when available, and report retrieval failures without guessing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: request a basic bulletin check.

prompt_templates.title: Look Up One Volcano
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the JMA warning for [volcano name]. Match its identifier to the master list and show the official warning label and publication time.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: identify and summarize a specific volcano.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Warnings and Commentary
prompt_templates.prompt: For [volcano name], compare its warning record with recent commentary headlines. Preserve publication times and distinguish older continuing warnings from new reports.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: combine separate sources without conflating their dates.

prompt_templates.title: Produce a Verified National Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve the four documented JMA feeds and join records by volcano identifier. Sort reports by publication time and list failed requests separately. Use official warning wording for affected areas; do not infer residential danger from level 3 alone.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare a cross-feed summary with explicit data-quality checks.

output_examples.input: The eruption feed was retrieved successfully and returned an empty list. Explain the result.
output: No eruption bulletins are currently listed in the retrieved feed.
An empty list is a valid response, not a retrieval error.
This does not establish that every volcano is safe or that no warning exists.

output_examples.input: Explain the skill's historical example: Aso, code 503, level 2, observed on September 19, 2026.
output: The documented example identifies Aso as volcano code 503 with a level 2 warning.
Level 2 indicates restrictions around the crater.
This is a historical observation, not a current status check.
Retrieve the current warning and include its publication time before reporting present conditions.

best_practices: Include each report's publication time and distinguish it from the time you retrieved the data.
Use the four documented endpoints and report failures instead of guessing replacement URLs or current conditions.
Verify affected areas and protective actions against official warning wording, especially when interpreting level 3 alerts.
anti_patterns: Treating an empty eruption bulletin feed as proof that volcano activity poses no danger.
Presenting historical examples or older continuing warnings as newly issued reports.
Inferring residential danger from an alert-level number alone or using the skill as an evacuation authority.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when the environment provides tools for retrieving public web data.

faq.question: Does it require an API key or login?
faq.answer: The documented JMA feeds require neither an API key nor a login. Your AI service and network access may have separate costs.

faq.question: Which information sources does it use?
faq.answer: It uses four public JMA feeds: eruption bulletins, eruption warnings, volcano commentary, and a volcano master list.

faq.question: Does it provide continuous live monitoring?
faq.answer: No. It guides on-demand retrieval and interpretation. The reviewed skill does not include a scheduler, notification service, or availability guarantee.

faq.question: What does an empty eruption feed mean?
faq.answer: After successful retrieval, an empty list means no eruption bulletins are listed. It does not mean there are no warnings or hazards.

faq.question: Can its alert summaries determine evacuation actions?
faq.answer: No. Its level 3 residential classification needs correction. Follow official JMA warning details and local authority instructions for protective actions.
